hook_text: Follow one R100 note through the shop. Watch who takes a cut.
clip_script: Take one hundred-rand note from the till and follow it as it breaks up. A customer hands it over for goods. First, the goods must be replaced: R80 goes straight back into stock. R20 remains — the margin, the money the shop actually gets to work with. Then the running of the shop takes its share: wages, telephone, insurance, the stock that went missing — nearly R17 of every hundred. The loan's interest nibbles its bit. And when everyone has taken their cut... R7,90 remains. From every single hundred that crossed the counter, the owner keeps seven rand ninety. That journey — 100 in, 80 replaced, 20 margin, 17 running, 8 kept — IS profitability analysis. The five official percentages are just checkpoint names along the note's journey. And here's why it matters: rand totals are trapped in their own year. Percentages travel — compare them with last year, with the shop across the road, with anyone. That's how numbers learn to talk.
visual_style: A single glowing R100 note travelling a conveyor through the shop, pieces splitting off at labelled checkpoints (80/20/17/7,90), the fragments forming a dashboard of five percentages at the end.
mood: Follow-the-money documentary energy, crisp and revelatory.
pacing: Continuous tracking motion with a beat at each split, closing on the dashboard snap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make your own numbers talk.
